hypotheses: Calibration is a kept feature of its own, not part of quote recovery (owner, 2026-11-03: "Keep both; record them as kept"). Calibration pairs JEV's score logged at judgment time with the owner's own labels: question-tool answers confirming or correcting an interpretation, approvals by the owner's words, and reversals labelled 'no' as P4 says. A record kind passes only with mixed evidence: at least 20 owner labels and 5 'no' examples, at most half generated, no 'no' wrongly accepted. Each run logs threshold, false-accept rate and recall with model version and prompt digest. No trial card asks for labels. A passing calibration raises the fast-track floor to its threshold; none is needed for the fast track (DEC-143).
given fewer than 20 labelled intents, when calibration runs, then the intent kind is not passing and intents are fast-tracked on the 0.9 floor alone
given a labelled set where one misread record got the judge's confidence 0.93, when calibration chooses the threshold, then the threshold is above 0.93

given no judge model is configured, when calibration runs (/iaso jev calibrate), then it reports that judging is unavailable, naming judgment.backend, exits with an error, and writes no calibration event

given the owner corrects the judge model's interpretation of SR-185 in the question tool, when calibration next runs, then the correction counts as a real 'no' paired with JEV's score logged at judgment time, with no new model call

given 25 requirement labels whose 5 'no' examples include 3 generated variations, when calibration runs, then the requirement kind is not passing, because more than half of its 'no' examples are generated

given the fast track off, no passing calibration, three records the judge model finds supported and one it finds beyond the owner's words, when the turn ends, then no trial or read-back card is shown; the supported records are not put to the owner and wait for JEV (SR-372), and only the one beyond goes the question route, the owner's answer becoming a label
